prompt:
Use case: style-transfer.
Asset type: replacement featured illustration for Tiny Brain on williswee.com/play.
Input image 1 is the EDIT TARGET: the user-supplied cute brain character. Preserve its identity and friendly appeal: two rounded brain hemispheres divided down the middle, simple curved brain folds, two bright oval eyes with highlights, rosy cheeks, a happy open smile, two little legs and feet, and two small arms EACH giving a thumbs-up. Keep the whole character and both thumbs clearly visible. No new characters.
Input image 2 is STYLE REFERENCE ONLY: Willis Wee's coastal pixel-art website illustration. Borrow the deliberate pixel clusters, limited softly dithered shading, midnight navy shadows, warm cream and lantern-gold highlights. Do not copy its scenery, people, buildings, sea, or layout.

Primary request: Turn the cute vector brain into a beautifully crafted retro adventure-game pixel-art mascot that belongs on this website. It should feel warm, personable and playful. Redraw every contour and feature in intentional square pixel clusters, with crisp stepped edges, coherent pixel scale and restrained handmade texture. This is a real artistic pixel-art reinterpretation, not a mosaic filter over the vector image.
Character palette: retain a recognisable warm peach/coral-pink brain, but make it less candy-bright and integrate the site's amber light. Use cream and pale peach highlights, muted rose shadow planes and deep indigo/navy contours. Eyes and smile are rich dark navy/plum; keep friendly white/cream eye glints. Small golden highlights add warmth, not metallic material.
Background: replace the lavender flat backdrop with quiet deep midnight navy #07101d. A handful of tiny cream and restrained gold pixel stars near the upper corners echo the source's sparkles. A subtle pixel-dithered grounding shadow below the feet. Keep the background simple and atmospheric, with clear separation from the character; no landscape and no extra props.
Composition: landscape approximately 3:2, ideally 1536 x 1024, to fit the site's project gallery. Center the complete character and let it occupy roughly 75% of the image height. Keep both hands, all fingers/raised thumbs, legs and feet within generous margins. The expression and thumbs should read instantly at 300 pixels wide. Keep the source's straight-on, slightly organic symmetrical pose.
Style finish: highly polished 1990s pixel-art game sprite illustration, dimensional but not a 3D render, crisp nearest-neighbour-like edges and hand-placed clusters. Do not smooth away the pixels. Midnight blue, muted coral, cream #f4e9cf and warm gold #ffbe63 form one coherent palette.
Text: none. No title, labels, letters, numbers, logos, watermark, frame or UI.
Avoid: photoreal anatomy, gore, neural-network wires, electric circuits, transparent brain, holograms, robots, human bodies, desks, books, kitchens, buildings, ocean, heavy neon glow, lens effects, smooth vector gradients, generic glossy 3D mascot, extra limbs, missing thumbs, extra faces or different expressions. Keep the user's cute thumbs-up brain as the sole subject.
